question: Are emergency vehicles  posted at the GW bridge?

answers: Yes, the George Washington Bridge has emergency vehicles stationed 24/7 at the bridge such as fire trucks , rescue trucks , and wreckers specially designed for the GW Bridge for serious incidents , such as fires , vehicle extrications , Haz - Mat incidents , overturned vehicles , and many other emergencies . Emergency Medical Services are also provided by the Agents .The Port Authority Police Department (PAPD) is responsible for law enforcement and security at the bridge, and they have patrol vehicles and officers deployed there to respond to emergencies and ensure the safety of the commuters and the bridge itself.

history.content: The George Washington Bridge, often abbreviated as GWB, GW, or simply the George, is a double-decked suspension bridge that spans the Hudson River. It connects the Washington Heights neighborhood of Manhattan in New York City with Fort Lee, New Jersey. The bridge is owned by the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey and, as of 2016, was the world's busiest motor vehicle bridge, carrying over 103 million vehicles per year.  In 1946 , two more lanes were created on the current upper level , widening it from the original six lanes . A second , lower deck , which had been anticipated in Ammann 's original plans , opened to the public on August 29 , 1962 . The lower level , nicknamed `` Martha '' after George 's wife Martha Washington , increased the capacity of the bridge by 75 percent , and simultaneously made the George Washington Bridge the world 's only 14 - lane suspension bridge. The George Washington Bridge has also been designated a National Historic Civil Engineering Landmark by the American Society of Civil Engineers. Unfortunately, it is also a common site for suicide attempts in the New York metropolitan area.

London Bridge is a bridge in Lake Havasu City , Arizona . It was built in the 1830s and formerly spanned the River Thames in London , England . It was dismantled in 1967 and relocated to Arizona . The Arizona bridge is a reinforced concrete structure clad in the original masonry of the 1830s bridge , which was purchased by Robert P. McCulloch from the City of London .
